hero.eyebrow: Church planting software, phase by phase
hero.headline: From calling to launch Sunday, one week at a time.
hero.subhead: Everyfield keeps your people, vision meetings, follow-ups and ministry teams in one place. It reads them against the Playbook and tells you what needs you this week.
hero.note: Everyfield is in early access. [[Say how access works, for example: invites go out through sending churches and networks.]]

problem.headline: A church launch has a hundred moving parts. Most of them live in your head.
problem.body: Three guests came to Thursday's vision meeting, and someone needs to call them by Saturday. Commitment cards sit in a folder. The kids ministry still has no leader. Your spreadsheet knows none of this, so the loudest problem gets your week, not the most important one.

proof.headline: Here is what a Monday looks like.
proof.body: Open Everyfield and the week is on one screen. Committed adults against the Playbook's benchmark of 50. Days since your last vision meeting against the 14-day rhythm. Follow-ups that are late, and who owns each one. One focus from Plant Intelligence, with the facts it used.
proof.visual: Dashboard crop from the round-buffalo mockup: TargetBar, the 'Needs you' list and one InsightCard.
proof.caption: Sample data. Harvest Point is a demo church.

features.headline: Everything a plant needs, in the order you need it.
features.intro: Everyfield follows the seven phases of the Playbook. Each phase brings its own work to the front.

items.label: Phase 0 · Discovery
items.title: Start with the method
items.body: Read the Playbook and Wiki in order. Everyfield opens the chapter for the phase you are in.

items.label: Phase 1 · Core group
items.title: Grow a committed core group
items.body: Track each person from first visit to signed commitment. Record interviews against the five considerations and the 4 Cs. When you close a vision meeting's attendance, Everyfield creates the follow-up tasks.

items.label: Phase 2 · Launch team
items.title: Set the date and fill the roles
items.body: Set launch day. See which of the eight ministry areas still has no leader, and who on your core group has the skills for it.

items.label: Phase 3 · Training
items.title: Train every team
items.body: Plan training meetings for each ministry team and see who has finished.

items.label: Phase 4 · Pre-launch
items.title: Finish the launch list
items.body: Work through launch milestones and their tasks. Send email to your people and print documents that already carry your church's details.

items.label: Phases 5 and 6 · Launch and after
items.title: Launch, then keep going
items.body: Record Launch Sunday and its outcome. Keep follow-up running when Sunday becomes a weekly rhythm.

audiences.headline: One plant. Three groups of people who care about it.

items.label: For networks
items.headline: Every plant in your network on one page.
items.body: Find the plants that need a call this month.
points: Each plant shows as on track, watch, launch readiness or limited visibility
Summaries only, and only what each plant chooses to share
The same method and the same rubric across every plant

evry.headline: Evry prepares the work. You approve it.
evry.body: Ask Evry who from last Thursday has no follow-up yet. It shows the list, with a link to each person. Ask it to assign those calls, and it prepares the tasks and waits. Nothing is saved until you approve the exact change on screen.

example.ask: Who from Thursday's vision meeting has no follow-up owner?
example.answer: Three first-time guests have no follow-up owner yet.
example.review: Review 3 changes · Assign follow-up calls · Approve or Edit

evry.limits: Evry does not write prayers, give counsel, judge a person's readiness or change your phase. It never reads your private check-in.

hero.headline: See how every plant you send is doing.
hero.subhead: Planters run their launch in Everyfield every day. You see a summary of each plant that shares with you: phase, health and launch readiness. You do not see their people.
hero.cta_primary: Talk to us about your network
hero.note: Everyfield is in early access. [[Say how access works for networks and for planters.]]

problem.headline: You usually hear about a struggling plant when it is already late.
problem.body: Reports come once a quarter, and each planter writes them a different way. A plant can go a month without a vision meeting before anyone outside notices. Coaches spend the first half of each call finding out what happened.

proof.headline: One row for each plant. One status you can act on.
proof.body: Each plant shows its phase, launch date and a health status: on track, watch, launch readiness or limited visibility. Limited visibility means the plant shares too little for a fair read, and Everyfield says that instead of guessing.
proof.visual: Oversight table: plant name, phase track, launch date, status badge. Use the mockup's StatusBadge and PhaseTrack components.
proof.caption: Sample data. All plant names are demo churches.

directions.name: The Playbook, put to work
directions.angle: The method made operational. The Playbook is the hero. Everyfield is how a planter follows it each week, and how anyone can check that they are.

hero.eyebrow: A church planting method you can run
hero.headline: The Playbook, put to work.
hero.subhead: Vision meetings every 14 days. Timely follow-up after each one. A core group of 50 to 100 committed adults. Eight ministry areas led before launch. Everyfield turns each step of the method into work you can see and finish.

problem.headline: A method in a binder cannot tell you that you are late.
problem.body: Most planters start with a good plan. Then the weeks fill up. Nobody notices that the last vision meeting was 16 days ago, or that half of Sunday's guests never got a call. The method stays right, and the plant drifts from it.

proof.headline: Your records, read against the method.
proof.body: Plant Intelligence checks your plant against the eight Critical Success Factors. It gives you one focus to work on, two more things to watch and what is going well. Every finding links to the facts it used and names the rubric version.
proof.visual: Plant Intelligence scorecard: eight CSF tiles and one focus card, built from the mockup's InsightCard and StatusBadge.
proof.caption: Sample data from a demo church.

features.headline: Each part of the method has a place in the product.
features.intro: Everyfield does not add steps to the Playbook. It gives each existing step a record, an owner and a date.

items.label: Vision meetings
items.title: Keep the rhythm
items.body: Plan each vision meeting, record attendance and see the days since the last one against the 14-day rhythm.

items.label: Follow-up
items.title: Follow up while it matters
items.body: Closing attendance creates a follow-up task for each new guest. Everyfield shows how many guests had contact within 48 hours of the meeting.

items.label: Commitments
items.title: Count committed adults
items.body: Record interviews against the five considerations and the 4 Cs: Committed, Compelled, Contagious, Courageous. Signed commitments count toward the benchmark of 50.

items.label: Ministry areas
items.title: Lead every area
items.body: Staff and train a team for each of the eight ministry areas, and see the gaps before launch.

items.label: Phases
items.title: Know where you are
items.body: Seven phases from Discovery to Post-Launch. You record your phase with a reason. Readiness is advice, never a gate.

items.label: Playbook and Wiki
items.title: Read the method in context
items.body: The chapter for your phase is one click from the work it describes.

audiences.headline: One method, read the same way by everyone.

evry.headline: Ask the method a question. Get your own records back.
evry.body: Ask Evry what the Playbook says about a first-time guest, and it shows the passage. Ask why your plant is on watch, and it explains the result against the rubric, with links to the records. Ask it to act, and it prepares the change for your approval.

example.ask: What does the Playbook say about follow-up after a vision meeting?
example.answer: The Playbook says timely follow-up is what grows the core group. Here is the passage, and here are the two guests from Thursday who have not had a call.
example.review: Review 2 changes · Create follow-up tasks · Approve or Edit

evry.limits: Evry quotes the method. It does not invent a benchmark, write prayers, give counsel or judge a person.

trust.headline: The software follows the method. It does not rewrite it.

items.title: Written by practitioners
items.body: The Playbook and the rubric come from church planting practitioners. [[Name the authors and their review.]]

items.title: Versioned rubric

items.title: Benchmarks, not verdicts
items.body: 50 to 100 committed adults is this method's benchmark, not a measure of whether a church is healthy.

items.title: People judge people
items.body: Interviews and the 4 Cs are your judgment. Plant Intelligence and Evry never fill them in.
